title: NCCL microburst and buffering study
content:
Purpose
This doc captures an ad-hoc investigation into short-lived (microburst) collective traffic patterns we observed during multi-GPU inference (tensor+pipeline hybrid) and how NCCL buffer sizing, kernel ordering, and driver-level coalescing affect end-to-end tail latency. The goal: identify practical mitigations to avoid 95th/99th token latency spikes without changing model sharding topology aggressively.

Background / Why this came up
- Multiple production incidents (late Sep 2024) where p99 token latency jumped 2–4x for 10–30s windows under steady qps.
- Traces pointed to sudden spikes in NCCL allreduce/collective time while other CPU/GPU metrics looked nominal.
- Hypothesis: small, frequent collective starts (microbursts) cause PCIe/NVLink buffer thrashing and serialization at HCA/NCCL level. Small message sizes + high fan-in create inefficient network utilization and queuing.

What we tested
1) Workloads: two representative inference workloads: a) short sequences (max_len=32) high concurrency (64 concurrent requests per node) b) long sequences (max_len=2048) low concurrency. Both used a 4xA100 node (8 GPUs) topology with tensor parallelism across GPUs and pipeline stages between nodes.
2) Topologies: local NVLink ring (intra-node), cross-node via NVSwitch+InfiniBand (8x100Gbps).
3) NCCL / driver variants: nccl 2.14 vs 2.16 (nightly), CUDA 11.8 vs 12.1, Linux rdma-core 46.
4) Buffer/control knobs: NCCL_BUFFSIZE (per-collective fragment), NCCL_BUFFS_PER_THREAD, NCCL_ALGO, NCCL_COLLNET_ENABLE, environment throttles (NCCL_DEBUG=INFO), PCIe ASPM off/on.
5) Tools: nvprof/nsight systems (nsys), ncu, ibv_devinfo, perf counters, custom nccl-tests microbench harness (modified to mimic our browse of small-sized collectives with variable inter-arrival times).

Microbench harness used
- Simulated collective fan-in/out of 8 GPUs with message sizes 4KB, 16KB, 64KB, 256KB.
- Controlled inter-arrival patterns: Poisson (lambda adjusted), batchy bursts (10ms window with 50% of total requests), and uniform steady arrival.
- Measured per-collective latency, NIC queues, and GPU kernel queue stalls.

Key observations
1) Microburst behavior is worst at message sizes in the 8–64KB range. For those sizes we saw 3–6x higher per-collective latency when arrivals were bursty vs steady with same aggregate throughput.
2) NCCL_BUFFSIZE tuning matters: default fragmenting created more small fragments for 8–64KB messages, increasing completion overhead. Increasing NCCL_BUFFSIZE reduced number of fragments and improved 95th latency by ~30% in several cases, but at the cost of higher mem footprint.
3) CollNet (collective offload) helped for large messages (>256KB) but showed no benefit for microburst small messages; in some cases it increased tail because it enforced ordering that serialized concurrent small collectives.
4) CUDA stream ordering + kernel launch patterns matter. If a GPU schedules many small kernels right before a collective start, it delays the kernel that performs the NCCL call (device-side enqueue latency increased). Reordering work to prioritize the collective kernel reduced microburst tail.
5) InfiniBand QP/RC-level queue depth and driver coalescing are a bottleneck: NIC counters showed queue buildup and periodic flushes consistent with microburst aggregation inside the HCA.
6) Enabling moderate software-level batching (buffer requests at application layer into per-model windows of 5–10ms) eliminated most spikes while only adding 1–2ms median latency — a worthwhile trade for interactive apps where p99 matters.

Representative numbers (4xA100, 8 GPUs, bursty window = 10ms)
- 16KB messages: steady arrival avg latency 0.85ms, p95 1.4ms; bursty arrival avg 0.9ms, p95 5.6ms, p99 11.2ms.
- Changing NCCL_BUFFSIZE -> 64KB: bursty p95 dropped to 3.8ms, p99 7.2ms.
- Application-level 5ms batching: p95 1.6ms, p99 2.5ms for the same bursty workload.

Commands / reproduction notes
- nccl-tests harness used (repo branch: nccl-microburst). Example run: 
  ./all_reduce_perf -b 16384 -e 16384 -f 2 -g 8 --iters 10000 (modified to drive arrival patterns)
- NCCL knobs exported before run: 
  export NCCL_BUFFSIZE=65536
  export NCCL_BUFFS_PER_THREAD=4
  export NCCL_ALGO=Ring
  export NCCL_DEBUG=WARN
- Profiling with nsys: 
  nsys profile --trace=cuda,nvtx --output=burst-16k nsys-target-binary
- ib counters: ibv_devinfo; ib_read_cq and tx counters observed during bursts.

Root causes (synthesis)
- Microbursts create a mismatch between message fragmentation (NCCL internal fragments) and NIC coalescing behavior. Small message bursts produce many small RDMA ops; the HCA coalesces and flushes based on internal heuristics, producing serialization and latency amplification.
- NCCL's per-thread fragment allocation and small default NCCL_BUFFSIZE lead to higher per-collective overhead under bursty small-message patterns.
- Application kernel ordering and stream priorities influence when the NCCL call actually enqueues on GPU; when many CUDA kernels queue up, the collective waits and then executes multiple collectives nearly simultaneously, worsening the burst.

Mitigations tried and trade-offs
1) Increase NCCL_BUFFSIZE (simple, low-effort): pros = immediate p99 improvement for small-messages; cons = more GPU pinned memory, possible negative effect on host-side latency if too large.
2) Application-side micro-batching (5–10ms windows): pros = best p95/p99 reduction; cons = added median latency, implementation required in request routing layer.
3) Prioritize collective launch kernels: use CUDA stream priorities or lightweight stream preemption. Pros = helps without impacting median; cons = more complex scheduling across pipeline stages.
4) Flow-control at network level (QP tuning): lower-level change, needs driver/kernel coordination and vendor support; pros = fundamental fix; cons = operationally heavy and may require vendor engagement.

Action items / next steps
- Short-term: enable NCCL_BUFFSIZE=65536 in the dedicated clusters used by short-seq workloads; run 72hr soak on prod-like traffic. (Assignee: Marco)
- Mid-term: implement minimal application-level 5ms batching in the request router (opt-in per-model). Add flag to Console to allow per-route micro-batching and show cost/latency trade-off. (Assignee: Priya)
- Investigate stream-priority enforcement within our runtime scheduler; prototype putting the collective-launching kernel on a high priority stream. (Assignee: Liam)
- File vendor ticket with NVIDIA/Cloud NIC team with trace captures and HCA counters; ask about HCA coalescing heuristics and whether firm-level firmware knobs exist to better handle many small RDMA ops. (Assignee: Evelyn)

Open questions
- What is the memory cost of a global change to NCCL_BUFFSIZE across our fleet with current model memory footprints? Need infra cost estimate.
- For pipeline-parallel models where collectives are correlated to stage boundaries, can we shift timing slightly to decorrelate microbursts without harming SLOs?
- Should we expose a runtime heuristic that switches buffering or collnet per message-size distribution? (e.g., if >70% messages <64KB, auto-enable app batching)

Appendix: quick checklist for reproducing in-house
- Use nccl-tests modified harness (branch: nccl-microburst).
- Match GPU topology and verify NVSwitch/IB settings identical to prod images.
- Record: nsys trace, ib counters, dmesg, and NCCL_TRACE logs.

Notes to reviewers
- This doc is intentionally pragmatic — the two short-term mitigations (NCCL_BUFFSIZE increase, opt-in 5ms batching) are low-risk and likely to materially reduce token-tail incidents. The vendor engagement will determine whether a deeper HCA-level fix is possible.
- Please comment with additional reproduction needs, or if you have NIC/firmware contacts who can help speed the ticket with vendor.
